title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages): Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators with generators ε_i (i = 0, 1, ∞). The underbrace on the page indicates l_1 = ε_1^2, which suggests a 'half-loop' or SL(2) normalisation. The neighbouring pages map a quotient to SL(2,Ẑ)', and ρ is the cyclic order-3 symmetry permuting the three points. M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] is a group of 'normalised' automorphisms u_ξ of Π̂_{0,3}. They are given by u_ξ(ε_0) = ε_0^μ and u_ξ(ε_1) = int(ξ)(ε_1^μ), with μ = 2ν+1 an odd profinite exponent and ξ in Π̂_{0,3}. These are subject to the 3-cycle relation ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ²(ξ) = 1, which is a hexagon-type condition. Composition is the twisted (cocycle) law u_{ξ'}u_ξ = u_{ξ''} with ξ'' = u_{ξ'}(ξ)ξ'. This is exactly the multiplication law (λ1,f1)(λ2,f2) = (λ1λ2, f1·φ1(f2)) of what is now called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT, extended by Z/2. τ is the nontrivial element of T_{0,3} ≅ Z/2, realised in the normalisation '(0)' as τ_∞ = u_{ξ'} with ξ' = l_1^{-1} and μ = -1, i.e. τ_∞(l_1) = l_1^{-1}. It is the 'complex conjugation' involution, corresponding to the GT element (λ,f) = (-1,1) up to normalisation. PROPOSITION: the centraliser of τ in N_{0,3}^{!~} is {1,τ}, i.e. complex conjugation is self-centralising. Proof sketch: (1) Commutation u_ξ τ_∞ = τ_∞ u_ξ is equivalent, by the composition law, to τ_∞(ξ) l_1^{-1} = u_ξ(l_1^{-1}) ξ, which is (61). (2) Using u_ξ(l_1^{-1}) = int(ξ)(l_1^{-μ}), this becomes ξ^{-1}τ_∞(ξ) = l_1^{1-μ} = l_1^{-2ν}, which is (62). (3) On the next page, ξ = l_1^ν is a solution. It is the unique one provided the fixed subgroup (Π̂_{0,3})^{τ_∞} is trivial, which is (64). Grothendieck explicitly ADMITS this, assuming that the discrete fact extends to the profinite case. (4) Imposing ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 on ξ = l_1^ν and passing to SL(2,Ẑ) gives, as on the previous page, 2ν+1 = μ = ±1. Hence ν ∈ {0,-1}, i.e. u ∈ {id, τ_∞}. A marginal note says the proposition is not used later (N° 46 VI only needs a weaker statement). In modern terms, this is the statement that complex conjugation c = (-1,1) has centraliser {1,c} in (the Z/2-extension of) ĜT. It is the GT analogue of the fact that complex conjugation is self-centralising in G_Q.
errors: The uniqueness step depends on (64), triviality of the fixed points of τ_∞ on the free profinite group Π̂_{0,3}. Grothendieck only assumes this by analogy with the discrete case ('si on admet que les résultats discrets se prolongent au cas profini'); it is not proved here. Geometrically, τ_∞ is complex conjugation based at a point of the real interval (0,1), whose real component is contractible. The discrete fixed group is plausibly trivial, but the profinite analogue needs a real argument (real-points / real-section type results).
On the next page the conclusion is written 'ν = ±1'. The computation on this page and the previous one (μ = 2ν+1 = ±1) gives ν ∈ {0, -1}, corresponding to u = id and u = τ_∞. '±1' is a slip.

The page speaks of the centraliser in N_{0,3}^{!~} (the normaliser group), but the computation is carried out only in the normalised subgroup M_{0,3}^{!~}[0], via the isomorphic copy N_{0,3}^{!~}(0). The passage from one to the other is only indicated, and the transcription of that sentence is partly illegible.

ideas.what: Composition law u_{ξ'}u_ξ = u_{ξ''} with ξ'' = u_{ξ'}(ξ)ξ' for automorphisms ε_1 ↦ int(ξ)ε_1^μ of the free profinite group on two generators.
ideas.modern_name: Multiplication law in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and the 'GT' idea, not these formulas

ideas.what: Self-centralising property of the complex-conjugation involution τ_∞ (λ = -1) in the GT-type group: its centraliser is {1, τ}.
ideas.modern_name: Centraliser of complex conjugation c = (-1,1) in ĜT is {1,c}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, 'The Grothendieck–Teichmüller group and automorphisms of braid groups' (1994) — I believe the centraliser statement is there, but unsure of exact attribution

ideas.what: Reduction of commutation to the twisted equation ξ^{-1}τ(ξ) = l_1^{-2ν}, together with the need for triviality of the τ-fixed subgroup of Π̂_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Fixed points of complex conjugation on the profinite π1 of a real curve (real points / real section-type statement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Profinite real-curve results (e.g. work around the real section conjecture: Pop, Wickelgren, Mochizuki) — unsure

ideas.what: Using the 3-cycle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 and its image in SL(2,Ẑ) to force μ = ±1 for ξ a power of a single loop.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon / 3-cycle relation of ĜT and its abelianised or SL2 image

missed.claim: Grothendieck states and essentially proves, apart from an admitted profinite fixed-point lemma, that complex conjugation is self-centralising in his version of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. This is a statement usually attributed to the 1990s GT literature (Lochak–Schneps) and is not credited to him.
missed.quote: Proposition Le commutant de τ (élément non trivial de T_{0,3} ≃ Z/2Z ⊂ M_{0,3}^{!~}) dans N_{0,3}^{!~} est réduit à {1,τ}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the ĜT group law and the analogue of the Artin–Schreier self-centralising property of complex conjugation were in Grothendieck's hands in the early 1980s, before Drinfeld and Ihara. This matters for the history of GT.

missed.claim: The profinite fixed-point lemma (Π̂_{0,3})^{τ_∞} = {1} is explicitly left as an assumption extrapolated from the discrete case.
missed.quote: si on admet que les résultats discrets se prolongent au cas profini, de façon à avoir (64) (Π̂_{0,3})^{τ_∞} = {1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean instance of the question of how fixed points of complex conjugation on profinite π1 relate to π1 of the real locus. This question is now handled by real-section-type techniques, so it is likely resolved.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows the ĜT composition law and the self-centralising property of complex conjugation, worked out in Grothendieck's own notation and predating Drinfeld and Lochak–Schneps. The result itself is known in the literature, and Grothendieck notes it is unused later. Its interest is mainly historical priority rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The margin note reads roughly: 'NB cette proposition n'est pas utilisée dans la suite (N° 46 VI, il suffit de l'énoncé ...)'.
The insertion reads 'où τ correspond à τ_∞'; it is an interlinear addition after N_{0,3}^{!~}(0).
The underbrace under l_1^{-1} reads ε_1^{-2}, i.e. l_1 = ε_1^2.
Read 'on fait' as 'en fait': 'en fait il a trouvé que le centralisateur de τ dans M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] formé entiers ...' (partly illegible).
